channel.title: Tech Strategy on Calyntro Blog
channel.description: Recent content in Tech Strategy on Calyntro Blog

item.title: Two Doors, One Gate: Navigating Governance Beyond EDD
item.description: Onboarding guardrails and power-user friction look like the same problem. They aren't. Here is why mixing awareness and governance at the developer level repeats a mistake we already made at the merge gate.

item.title: What Your Git History Reveals About Team Alignment
item.description: Your org chart shows who should own what. Your git history shows who actually does. They're rarely the same — and the gap is readable. Here's how.

item.title: EDD Closes the Loop — But Only Half of It
item.description: Expectation-Driven Development is a genuine step forward for AI-assisted development. But it solves the wrong half of the problem. Here is what the other half requires.

item.title: Knowledge Risk: From Metric to Recommended Action
item.description: Most tools tell you that knowledge is concentrated. Calyntro tells you what to do about it — and why some risks are more urgent than they appear when you combine ownership data with change coupling.

item.title: Bad Sprints Start Before the Sprint
item.description: Teams blame the board when sprints go sideways. The actual problem is almost always in refinement — and it starts long before the sprint does.

item.title: Conway's Law Is Already in Your Commit History
item.description: Conway's Law has been treated as a design principle for 58 years. It's time to treat it as something measurable — and your Git history already has the data.

item.title: Was Ihre Git-Historie über Ihr Team verrät — und warum kaum jemand hinschaut
item.description: 5 Risikosignale in jeder Codebase — Hotspots, Wissenssilos, Change Coupling. Sie stehen bereits in Ihrer Git-Historie. Kaum ein Team liest sie systematisch.

item.title: How to Measure Bus Factor in Your Software Team
item.description: Bus factor tells you how many people you can lose before a project stalls. Most teams guess. Here's how to measure it directly from Git history — no surveys, no interviews.

item.title: The Last Mile Problem in AI-Assisted Development
item.description: AI reviews can flag issues. But flags are not gates. The last mile — from finished code to trusted repository — is still unsolved. Here is why, and what actually helps.

item.title: What Calyntro Measures — And Why Standard Tools Miss It
item.description: Most ownership tools answer who last touched a file. Calyntro asks a harder question: who would be left holding it if the person who built it walked out the door tomorrow?

item.title: From Chaos to Coherence: What AI Cannot Do for Your Architecture
item.description: AI builds fast. But coherence is the architect's job — not the AI's. A concrete story of PoC chaos, a full reset, and what only humans can define in a system.

item.title: What We Found When We Analysed MongoDB's Codebase
item.description: A file can look shared today but have been built entirely by someone who left last year. We ran that analysis on MongoDB — and the results are worth paying attention to.

item.title: The Invisible Risk in Your Codebase
item.description: Most teams know that critical knowledge is concentrated in a few people. Almost none know exactly where. That's not a knowledge transfer problem — it's a visibility problem.

item.title: The Parallelization Paradox: Why Speed is Killing Your Agility
item.description: Why optimizing for simultaneous output with coding agents often leads back to a rigid Waterfall mindset.
